Listing 3.33 Complete replsim/src/main.rs. replsim/src/main.rs

//! Command replsim runs a leader and 2 followers in one process and carries
//! the messages between them by hand, so that it can lose any message it
//! chooses. It first walks through the cases of the chapter, and then tries
//! every combination of lost requests and lost answers over 3 writes and
//! checks what the replicas hold after each.
//!
//! Run it from code/ with:
//!
//!     cargo run --release -p replsim

use std::env;
use std::error::Error;
use std::fs;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::process;

use kv::{Change, Condition};
use repl::{Replica, majority_sequence};

/// What happens to one exchange between the leader and a follower.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Fate {
    Delivered,
    /// The follower does not receive the message.
    RequestLost,
    /// The follower processes the message, and its answer does not arrive.
    AnswerLost,
}

/// A leader, 2 followers, and what the leader knows about each follower.
struct Cluster {
    leader: Replica,
    followers: Vec<Replica>,
    /// The last sequence each follower has reported.
    reported: Vec<u64>,
}

impl Cluster {
    fn open(root: &Path) -> Result<Cluster, Box<dyn Error>> {
        let open = |name: &str| Replica::open(&root.join(name), false, 1);

        Ok(Cluster {
            leader: open("leader")?,
            followers: vec![open("follower-1")?, open("follower-2")?],
            reported: vec![0, 0],
        })
    }

    /// One exchange with a follower: the leader sends what the follower
    /// lacks, as far as it knows, and commits what a majority now holds.
    fn exchange(&mut self, follower: usize, fate: Fate) -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> {
        let message = self
            .leader
            .append_for(self.reported[follower]);

        if fate == Fate::RequestLost {
            return Ok(());
        }

        let answer = self.followers[follower].handle_append(message)?;

        if fate == Fate::AnswerLost {
            return Ok(());
        }

        self.reported[follower] = answer.last_sequence;

        let stored = vec![
            self.leader.last_sequence(),
            self.reported[0],
            self.reported[1],
        ];
        self.leader
            .commit(majority_sequence(stored));

        Ok(())
    }

    /// A write: the leader appends the record and makes one exchange with
    /// each follower. It returns whether the write was acknowledged, or
    /// `None` when the leader could not accept it.
    fn write(
        &mut self,
        key: &str,
        value: &str,
        fates: [Fate; 2],
    ) -> Result<Option<bool>, Box<dyn Error>> {
        if !self.leader.is_settled() {
            return Ok(None);
        }

        let change = Change::Put {
            key: key.into(),
            value: value.into(),
        };
        let sequence = self
            .leader
            .propose(change, Condition::Always)?;

        self.exchange(0, fates[0])?;
        self.exchange(1, fates[1])?;

        Ok(Some(self.leader.committed() >= sequence))
    }

    /// The last sequence of the leader and of each follower.
    fn lasts(&self) -> [u64; 3] {
        [
            self.leader.last_sequence(),
            self.followers[0].last_sequence(),
            self.followers[1].last_sequence(),
        ]
    }
}

const BOTH: [Fate; 2] = [Fate::Delivered, Fate::Delivered];

fn cases(root: &Path) -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> {
    let mut cluster = Cluster::open(root)?;
    let show = |cluster: &Cluster| {
        format!(
            "logs end at {:?}, committed {}",
            cluster.lasts(),
            cluster.leader.committed()
        )
    };

    for key in ["a", "b", "c"] {
        cluster.write(key, "1", BOTH)?;
    }

    println!("3 writes, every message delivered: {}", show(&cluster));

    for key in ["d", "e", "f"] {
        cluster.write(key, "1", [Fate::RequestLost, Fate::Delivered])?;
    }

    println!(
        "3 writes while follower 1 is unreachable: {}",
        show(&cluster)
    );

    cluster.exchange(0, Fate::Delivered)?;
    println!("follower 1 returns, 1 exchange: {}", show(&cluster));

    for key in ["g", "h", "i"] {
        cluster.write(key, "1", [Fate::AnswerLost, Fate::Delivered])?;
    }

    println!(
        "3 writes while the answers of follower 1 are lost: {}",
        show(&cluster)
    );
    println!(
        "  the leader believes that the log of follower 1 ends at {}",
        cluster.reported[0]
    );

    cluster.exchange(0, Fate::Delivered)?;
    println!(
        "  next exchange: the leader sends records 7 to 9, follower 1 refuses and reports {}",
        cluster.reported[0]
    );

    cluster.exchange(0, Fate::Delivered)?;
    println!("  the exchange after it: {}", show(&cluster));

    let acknowledged =
        cluster.write("j", "1", [Fate::RequestLost, Fate::RequestLost])? == Some(true);
    println!(
        "1 write while both followers are unreachable: acknowledged {acknowledged}, {}",
        show(&cluster)
    );
    println!(
        "  the leader reads j as {:?}",
        cluster
            .leader
            .get("j")
            .map(|entry| entry.version)
    );

    let accepted = cluster
        .write("k", "1", [Fate::RequestLost, Fate::RequestLost])?
        .is_some();
    println!("  the leader accepts another write: {accepted}");

    cluster.exchange(1, Fate::Delivered)?;
    println!("follower 2 returns: {}", show(&cluster));
    println!(
        "  the leader reads j as {:?}",
        cluster
            .leader
            .get("j")
            .map(|entry| entry.version)
    );

    let mut newer = Replica::open(&root.join("newer"), false, 2)?;
    let answer = newer.handle_append(cluster.leader.append_for(0))?;
    println!(
        "a replica at term 2 receives a message of term 1: appended {}, its term {}",
        answer.appended, answer.term
    );

    Ok(())
}

const WRITES: usize = 3;

/// The fate of exchange number `index` under a pattern: 2 bits for each.
fn fate(pattern: u32, index: usize) -> Fate {
    match (pattern >> (2 * index)) & 3 {
        0 | 1 => Fate::Delivered,
        2 => Fate::RequestLost,
        3.. => Fate::AnswerLost,
    }
}

/// Runs 3 writes under one pattern of losses and checks the replicas. It
/// returns the number of writes that were acknowledged.
fn run(root: &Path, pattern: u32) -> Result<usize, Box<dyn Error>> {
    let mut cluster = Cluster::open(root)?;
    let mut acknowledged = Vec::new();

    for number in 0..WRITES {
        let fates = [fate(pattern, 2 * number), fate(pattern, 2 * number + 1)];

        if cluster.write(&format!("key-{number}"), "1", fates)? == Some(true) {
            acknowledged.push(cluster.leader.last_sequence());
        }
    }

    for &sequence in &acknowledged {
        let holders = cluster
            .lasts()
            .iter()
            .filter(|&&last| last >= sequence)
            .count();

        if holders < 2 {
            return Err(format!(
                "pattern {pattern}: record {sequence} was acknowledged and is in {holders} log"
            )
            .into());
        }
    }

    for follower in &cluster.followers {
        if !cluster
            .leader
            .records()
            .starts_with(follower.records())
        {
            return Err(format!(
                "pattern {pattern}: a follower's log is not the beginning of the leader's"
            )
            .into());
        }
    }

    for _ in 0..2 {
        cluster.exchange(0, Fate::Delivered)?;
        cluster.exchange(1, Fate::Delivered)?;
    }

    let [leader, first, second] = cluster.lasts();

    if first != leader || second != leader || !cluster.leader.is_settled() {
        return Err(format!(
            "pattern {pattern}: the logs differ after every message was delivered"
        )
        .into());
    }

    Ok(acknowledged.len())
}

fn exhaustive(root: &Path) -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> {
    let patterns = 1u32 << (4 * WRITES);
    let mut by_acknowledged = [0; WRITES + 1];

    for pattern in 0..patterns {
        let directory = root.join(format!("pattern-{pattern}"));
        by_acknowledged[run(&directory, pattern)?] += 1;
        fs::remove_dir_all(&directory)?;
    }

    println!("{patterns} patterns of lost messages over {WRITES} writes:");
    println!("  every acknowledged record was in at least 2 of the 3 logs");
    println!("  every follower's log was the beginning of the leader's log");
    println!("  after the losses stopped, the 3 logs were equal and every record was committed");

    for (count, patterns) in by_acknowledged.iter().enumerate() {
        println!("  {count} of {WRITES} writes acknowledged: {patterns} patterns");
    }

    Ok(())
}

fn directory() -> PathBuf {
    env::temp_dir().join(format!("replsim-{}", process::id()))
}

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> {
    let root = directory();
    let result = cases(&root.join("cases")).and_then(|()| exhaustive(&root));

    fs::remove_dir_all(&root)?;

    result
}

//! The replication service: the generated gRPC types, the conversion between
//! them and the types of the `repl` crate, and the server side that a
//! follower runs.

use std::sync::Arc;

use kv::{Change, Record};
use repl::{Append, Appended};
use tokio::task;
use tonic::{Request, Response, Status};

use crate::node::Node;

/// The types that `build.rs` generates from `proto/store.proto`. The schema
/// also defines the ring, which this program does not use.
#[allow(dead_code)]
pub mod proto {
    tonic::include_proto!("store.v1");
}

pub use proto::replication_client::ReplicationClient;
pub use proto::replication_server::{Replication, ReplicationServer};

impl From<&Record> for proto::Record {
    fn from(record: &Record) -> Self {
        let change = match record.change.clone() {
            Change::Put { key, value } => proto::record::Change::Put(proto::Put { key, value }),
            Change::Delete { key } => proto::record::Change::Delete(proto::Delete { key }),
        };

        proto::Record {
            sequence: record.sequence,
            change: Some(change),
        }
    }
}

impl TryFrom<proto::Record> for Record {
    type Error = Status;

    fn try_from(record: proto::Record) -> Result<Self, Status> {
        let change = match record.change {
            Some(proto::record::Change::Put(put)) => Change::Put {
                key: put.key,
                value: put.value,
            },
            Some(proto::record::Change::Delete(delete)) => Change::Delete { key: delete.key },
            None => return Err(Status::invalid_argument("a record without a change")),
        };

        Ok(Record {
            sequence: record.sequence,
            change,
        })
    }
}

impl From<Append> for proto::AppendRequest {
    fn from(message: Append) -> Self {
        proto::AppendRequest {
            shard: 0,
            term: message.term,
            previous_sequence: message.previous_sequence,
            records: message
                .records
                .iter()
                .map(proto::Record::from)
                .collect(),
            committed_sequence: message.committed_sequence,
            // The fields that leader election added are not used by this program.
            previous_term: 0,
            leader: 0,
        }
    }
}

impl From<proto::AppendResponse> for Appended {
    fn from(answer: proto::AppendResponse) -> Self {
        Appended {
            term: answer.term,
            appended: answer.appended,
            last_sequence: answer.last_sequence,
        }
    }
}

/// The server side of `Append`, which a follower runs.
pub struct Follower {
    pub node: Arc<Node>,
}

#[tonic::async_trait]
impl Replication for Follower {
    async fn append(
        &self,
        request: Request<proto::AppendRequest>,
    ) -> Result<Response<proto::AppendResponse>, Status> {
        let request = request.into_inner();
        let records = request
            .records
            .into_iter()
            .map(Record::try_from)
            .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;

        let message = Append {
            term: request.term,
            previous_sequence: request.previous_sequence,
            records,
            committed_sequence: request.committed_sequence,
        };

        // Appending waits for the disk, so it runs where blocking is allowed.
        let answer = task::block_in_place(|| {
            self.node
                .replica
                .lock()
                .handle_append(message)
        })
        .map_err(|error| Status::unavailable(error.to_string()))?;

        Ok(Response::new(proto::AppendResponse {
            term: answer.term,
            appended: answer.appended,
            last_sequence: answer.last_sequence,
        }))
    }
}

Listing 3.36 Complete kvnode/src/node.rs. kvnode/src/node.rs

//! A node of a replicated shard: a replica, and for a leader the tasks that
//! keep its followers up to date.

use std::sync::Arc;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicU64, Ordering};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use kv::{Change, Condition, Entry, Summary, Written};
use kvd::api::ApiError;
use parking_lot::Mutex;
use repl::{Appended, Replica, majority_sequence};
use tokio::sync::{Notify, watch};
use tokio::task;
use tokio::time::{sleep, timeout};
use tonic::transport::{Channel, Endpoint};

use crate::rpc::{ReplicationClient, proto};

/// How often a leader sends a message to a follower that has nothing new to receive.
const HEARTBEAT: Duration = Duration::from_millis(100);

/// How long a leader waits for the answer to one message.
const ANSWER: Duration = Duration::from_millis(500);

/// How long a write waits for its record to reach a majority.
const COMMIT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(1);

/// What the leader knows about one follower.
pub struct Peer {
    pub address: String,
    /// The last sequence the follower has reported.
    reported: AtomicU64,
    /// When the follower last answered.
    heard: Mutex<Option<Instant>>,
}

pub struct Node {
    pub replica: Mutex<Replica>,
    pub leader: bool,
    pub peers: Vec<Peer>,
    /// The sequence the log ended at when the node started. A leader serves
    /// reads once this much is committed.
    ready: u64,
    /// Held by the write that is in progress, so that writes take turns.
    turn: tokio::sync::Mutex<()>,
    /// The committed sequence, for writes that wait for it to advance.
    committed: watch::Sender<u64>,
    /// Signalled when the leader has appended a record.
    appended: Notify,
    /// Set when a follower answers with a newer term: another leader exists.
    deposed: AtomicBool,
}

impl Node {
    pub fn new(replica: Replica, leader: bool, followers: Vec<String>) -> Arc<Node> {
        let peer = |address| Peer {
            address,
            reported: AtomicU64::new(0),
            heard: Mutex::new(None),
        };

        Arc::new(Node {
            ready: replica.last_sequence(),
            replica: Mutex::new(replica),
            leader,
            peers: followers
                .into_iter()
                .map(peer)
                .collect(),
            turn: tokio::sync::Mutex::new(()),
            committed: watch::Sender::new(0),
            appended: Notify::new(),
            deposed: AtomicBool::new(false),
        })
    }
}

impl Node {
    /// Starts one task for each follower. A task sends the follower what it
    /// lacks, again and again, for as long as the node runs.
    pub fn lead(self: &Arc<Node>) -> Result<(), tonic::transport::Error> {
        for index in 0..self.peers.len() {
            let channel = Endpoint::from_shared(self.peers[index].address.clone())?
                .connect_timeout(ANSWER)
                .connect_lazy();

            tokio::spawn(Arc::clone(self).follow(index, ReplicationClient::new(channel)));
        }

        Ok(())
    }

    async fn follow(self: Arc<Node>, index: usize, mut client: ReplicationClient<Channel>) {
        let peer = &self.peers[index];

        loop {
            let message = self.replica.lock().append_for(
                peer.reported
                    .load(Ordering::Relaxed),
            );
            let request = proto::AppendRequest::from(message);

            let answer = timeout(ANSWER, client.append(request)).await;

            // An answer that did not come counts as a peer that is up to date:
            // the next round is a heartbeat, which finds out more.
            let behind = answer
                .ok()
                .and_then(Result::ok)
                .is_some_and(|answer| self.record(peer, answer.into_inner().into()));

            if !behind {
                // Wait for a new record, or send a heartbeat when none comes.
                tokio::select! {
                    () = self.appended.notified() => {}
                    () = sleep(HEARTBEAT) => {}
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

impl Node {
    /// Takes note of a follower's answer and commits what a majority now
    /// holds. It returns whether the follower still lacks records.
    fn record(&self, peer: &Peer, answer: Appended) -> bool {
        let mut replica = self.replica.lock();

        if answer.term > replica.term() {
            self.deposed
                .store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);

            return false;
        }

        peer.reported
            .store(answer.last_sequence, Ordering::Relaxed);
        *peer.heard.lock() = Some(Instant::now());

        let mut stored: Vec<u64> = self
            .peers
            .iter()
            .map(|peer| {
                peer.reported
                    .load(Ordering::Relaxed)
            })
            .collect();
        stored.push(replica.last_sequence());

        replica.commit(majority_sequence(stored));
        self.committed
            .send_replace(replica.committed());

        answer.last_sequence < replica.last_sequence()
    }
}

impl Node {
    /// A write on the leader: wait for a turn, append the record, and wait
    /// until a majority of the replicas hold it.
    pub async fn write(&self, change: Change, condition: Condition) -> Result<Written, ApiError> {
        self.must_lead()?;

        let turn = self.turn.lock().await;
        let last = self.replica.lock().last_sequence();
        self.wait_for(last).await?;

        let proposed = task::block_in_place(|| {
            let mut replica = self.replica.lock();
            let created = match &change {
                Change::Put { key, .. } | Change::Delete { key } => replica.get(key).is_none(),
            };

            replica
                .propose(change, condition)
                .map(|version| Written { version, created })
        })?;

        self.appended.notify_waiters();
        self.wait_for(proposed.version)
            .await?;
        drop(turn);

        Ok(proposed)
    }

    /// Waits until the record with this sequence is committed.
    async fn wait_for(&self, sequence: u64) -> Result<(), ApiError> {
        let mut committed = self.committed.subscribe();

        let reached = committed.wait_for(|&committed| committed >= sequence);
        let in_time = timeout(COMMIT, reached)
            .await
            .is_ok_and(|reached| reached.is_ok());

        if in_time {
            Ok(())
        } else {
            Err(ApiError::Unavailable(format!(
                "record {sequence} is not on a majority of the replicas"
            )))
        }
    }

    fn must_lead(&self) -> Result<(), ApiError> {
        if !self.leader {
            return Err(ApiError::Misdirected("this node is a follower".into()));
        }

        if self.deposed.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
            return Err(ApiError::Misdirected(
                "a leader of a newer term exists".into(),
            ));
        }

        Ok(())
    }
}

impl Node {
    /// A leader serves reads while a majority of the replicas, itself
    /// included, has answered within the last second, and once everything
    /// its log held at start is committed.
    fn must_serve_reads(&self) -> Result<(), ApiError> {
        self.must_lead()?;

        let recently = |peer: &&Peer| {
            peer.heard
                .lock()
                .is_some_and(|at| at.elapsed() < COMMIT)
        };
        let reachable = 1 + self
            .peers
            .iter()
            .filter(recently)
            .count();

        if 2 * reachable <= self.peers.len() + 1 {
            return Err(ApiError::Unavailable(
                "this leader cannot reach a majority of the replicas".into(),
            ));
        }

        if self.replica.lock().committed() < self.ready {
            return Err(ApiError::Unavailable(
                "the records from before the restart are not committed yet".into(),
            ));
        }

        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Result<Entry, ApiError> {
        self.must_serve_reads()?;

        self.replica
            .lock()
            .get(key)
            .cloned()
            .ok_or(ApiError::NotFound)
    }

    pub fn list(
        &self,
        prefix: &str,
        after: Option<&str>,
        limit: usize,
    ) -> Result<(Vec<Summary>, bool), ApiError> {
        self.must_serve_reads()?;

        Ok(self
            .replica
            .lock()
            .list(prefix, after, limit))
    }

    /// The last sequence each follower has reported.
    pub fn reported(&self) -> Vec<u64> {
        self.peers
            .iter()
            .map(|peer| {
                peer.reported
                    .load(Ordering::Relaxed)
            })
            .collect()
    }
}

Listing 3.37 presents the complete HTTP server entry point and CLI runner in kvnode/src/main.rs.

Listing 3.37 Complete kvnode/src/main.rs. kvnode/src/main.rs

//! Command kvnode is a storage node that replicates its log. One node of a
//! shard is started as the leader, with the addresses of its followers, and
//! the others as followers. The leader serves the HTTP API and acknowledges
//! a write when a majority of the nodes hold its record.
//!
//! Run 3 nodes from code/ with:
//!
//!     cargo run -p kvnode -- --role follower --listen 127.0.0.1:7002 --replication 127.0.0.1:7102 --data /var/tmp/n2
//!     cargo run -p kvnode -- --role follower --listen 127.0.0.1:7003 --replication 127.0.0.1:7103 --data /var/tmp/n3
//!     cargo run -p kvnode -- --role leader --listen 127.0.0.1:7001 --data /var/tmp/n1 \
//!         --follower http://127.0.0.1:7102 --follower http://127.0.0.1:7103

mod node;
mod rpc;

use axum::http::header::{CONTENT_TYPE, ETAG, IF_NONE_MATCH};
use axum::http::{HeaderMap, StatusCode};
use axum::response::{IntoResponse, Response};
use axum::routing::get;
use axum::{Json, Router};
use clap::{Parser, ValueEnum};
use kv::{Change, Condition};
use kvd::api::{ApiError, MAX_VALUE, etag, valid_key, version_header, write_condition};

use crate::rpc::{Follower, ReplicationServer};

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, ValueEnum)]
enum Role {
    Leader,
    Follower,
}

#[derive(Parser)]
struct Options {
    #[arg(long, value_enum)]
    role: Role,

    /// The address of the HTTP API.
    #[arg(long, default_value = "127.0.0.1:7001")]
    listen: SocketAddr,

    /// The address on which a follower accepts records from the leader.
    #[arg(long, default_value = "127.0.0.1:7101")]
    replication: SocketAddr,

    /// The replication address of a follower, such as http://127.0.0.1:7102.
    /// Given once for each follower, to the leader.
    #[arg(long = "follower")]
    followers: Vec<String>,

    /// The term this node starts in. A new leader is given a higher term
    /// than the leader it replaces.
    #[arg(long, default_value_t = 1)]
    term: u64,

    #[arg(long, default_value = "data")]
    data: PathBuf,

    /// Respond without waiting for the disk.
    #[arg(long)]
    no_sync: bool,
}

async fn put_key(
    State(node): State<Arc<Node>>,
    Path(key): Path<String>,
    headers: HeaderMap,
    body: Bytes,
) -> Result<Response, ApiError> {
    valid_key(&key)?;
    let condition = write_condition(&headers)?;

    let written = node
        .write(
            Change::Put {
                key,
                value: body.to_vec(),
            },
            condition,
        )
        .await?;
    let status = if written.created {
        StatusCode::CREATED
    } else {
        StatusCode::NO_CONTENT
    };

    Ok((status, [(ETAG, etag(written.version))]).into_response())
}

async fn delete_key(
    State(node): State<Arc<Node>>,
    Path(key): Path<String>,
    headers: HeaderMap,
) -> Result<StatusCode, ApiError> {
    valid_key(&key)?;
    let condition = write_condition(&headers)?;

    node.write(Change::Delete { key }, condition)
        .await?;

    Ok(StatusCode::NO_CONTENT)
}

async fn get_key(
    State(node): State<Arc<Node>>,
    Path(key): Path<String>,
    headers: HeaderMap,
) -> Result<Response, ApiError> {
    valid_key(&key)?;
    let cached = version_header(&headers, IF_NONE_MATCH)?;
    let entry = node.get(&key)?;
    let tag = [(ETAG, etag(entry.version))];

    if cached == Some(Condition::Version(entry.version)) {
        return Ok((StatusCode::NOT_MODIFIED, tag).into_response());
    }

    Ok((
        tag,
        [(CONTENT_TYPE, "application/octet-stream")],
        entry.value,
    )
        .into_response())
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct ListQuery {
    #[serde(default)]
    prefix: String,
    after: Option<String>,
    limit: Option<usize>,
}

#[derive(Serialize)]
struct Item {
    key: String,
    version: u64,
    size: usize,
}

#[derive(Serialize)]
struct Page {
    keys: Vec<Item>,
    next_after: Option<String>,
}

async fn list_keys(
    State(node): State<Arc<Node>>,
    Query(query): Query<ListQuery>,
) -> Result<Json<Page>, ApiError> {
    let limit = query
        .limit
        .unwrap_or(100)
        .clamp(1, 1000);
    let (page, more) = node.list(&query.prefix, query.after.as_deref(), limit)?;
    let next_after = if more {
        page.last()
            .map(|last| last.key.clone())
    } else {
        None
    };
    let keys = page
        .into_iter()
        .map(|item| Item {
            key: item.key,
            version: item.version,
            size: item.size,
        })
        .collect();

    Ok(Json(Page { keys, next_after }))
}

#[derive(Serialize)]
struct Health {
    role: &'static str,
    term: u64,
    last_sequence: u64,
    committed: u64,
    /// The last sequence each follower has reported to this leader.
    followers: Vec<u64>,
}

async fn health(State(node): State<Arc<Node>>) -> Json<Health> {
    let replica = node.replica.lock();

    Json(Health {
        role: if node.leader { "leader" } else { "follower" },
        term: replica.term(),
        last_sequence: replica.last_sequence(),
        committed: replica.committed(),
        followers: node.reported(),
    })
}

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> {
    let options = Options::parse();
    let replica = Replica::open(&options.data, !options.no_sync, options.term)?;

    println!(
        "term {}, log ends at {}",
        replica.term(),
        replica.last_sequence()
    );

    let node = Node::new(replica, options.role == Role::Leader, options.followers);

    match options.role {
        Role::Leader => node.lead()?,
        Role::Follower => {
            let service = ReplicationServer::new(Follower {
                node: Arc::clone(&node),
            });

            tokio::spawn(
                Server::builder()
                    .add_service(service)
                    .serve(options.replication),
            );
            println!("accepting records on {}", options.replication);
        }
    }

    let routes = Router::new()
        .route("/v1/keys", get(list_keys))
        .route(
            "/v1/keys/{key}",
            get(get_key)
                .put(put_key)
                .delete(delete_key),
        )
        .route("/healthz", get(health))
        .layer(DefaultBodyLimit::max(MAX_VALUE))
        .with_state(node);

    let listener = TcpListener::bind(options.listen).await?;
    println!("listening on {}", listener.local_addr()?);

    axum::serve(listener, routes).await?;

    Ok(())
}

Further Reading

  • B. Oki and B. Liskov, “Viewstamped Replication: A New Primary Copy Method to Support Highly-Available Distributed Systems”, PODC 1988.
  • D. Ongaro and J. Ousterhout, “In Search of an Understandable Consensus Algorithm”, USENIX ATC 2014.
  • R. van Renesse and F. Schneider, “Chain Replication for Supporting High Throughput and Availability”, OSDI 2004.

Summary

  • A shard leader streams missing WAL suffixes via Append RPCs tagged with term, previous_sequence, and committed_sequence.
  • A follower appends only when request.term >= local.term and request.previous_sequence == local.last_sequence, reporting its own last_sequence unconditionally on every reply so restarted, empty, or lagging followers realign in one round trip.
  • The leader computes the committed watermark via majority_sequence (the median of all replica log frontiers sorted descending) and applies only committed records to the in-memory BTreeMap.
  • Deterministic fault simulation (replsim) verified invariants 0 and 1 across all 4,096 combinations of dropped requests and dropped replies over three writes.
  • An error returned during quorum loss (503) signifies an indeterminate write whose local WAL record can still commit later upon quorum restoration.
  • Releasing the replica mutex before awaiting gRPC replies prevents a partitioned follower from stalling the surviving majority.
  • Live three-node experiments confirmed zero write interruption on single-follower crash, PC/EC refusal on quorum loss, zero loss of 228 acknowledged writes upon permanent leader disk destruction, and immediate 421 fencing of a returning term 1 leader.

Chapter 4: Raft Leader Election and Fencing (LLD)

In Chapter 3, an operator appointed each shard’s leader manually, and when a leader failed the shard rejected every write until someone inspected follower health endpoints and promoted a survivor by hand. Non-functional requirement 2 of Chapter 1 permits at most 21.6 minutes of unavailability per 30-day month (99.95% availability). No manual incident-response workflow can stay within that budget across dozens of shards. The replicas of a shard must elect their own leader automatically.

Stated concisely, automated failover sounds modest; in practice, it is the hardest algorithmic problem in this book. The members of a shard must converge on a single leader even though they communicate solely over an asynchronous network that drops and delays messages, any replica may crash and restart with only its persisted disk state, and no replica can distinguish a crashed peer from a slow or partitioned peer. Two members must never lead the same term concurrently, because split leadership would allow divergent writes. Moreover, every elected leader must already hold every write acknowledged in earlier terms so that new writes never overwrite durable client state. Reaching agreement under these fault assumptions is the problem of distributed consensus.

In this chapter, I implement the Raft consensus algorithm (Ongaro and Ousterhout, 2014) in Rust, extending the replication engine of Chapter 3 with persistent voting, term-tagged log matching, uncommitted suffix truncation, and current-term commit rules. We first build raft as a pure, clock-free, network-free state-machine library so we can drive deterministic fault injection in raftsim across 200 randomized runs of 600 steps and validate the simulator itself by disabling safety rules one by one. We then wrap raft in the networked server kvraft over gRPC and HTTP, and measure real failover pause duration under continuous write load (probe) when killing an active leader with SIGKILL.

In this chapter, we cover

  • the three Raft server roles (Follower, Candidate, Leader) and monotonic term transitions
  • volatile versus durable state (kv.log plus atomic state persistence for term and voted_for)
  • deterministic per-term election timeouts and the three-part Raft voting rule
  • zero-schema-change term markers that encode record terms inside the Chapter 2 WAL and commit inherited logs
  • Raft Log Matching (previous_term), suffix conflict resolution, and safe truncation of uncommitted records
  • the current-term commit rule and why counting replicas on earlier-term records is unsafe
  • deterministic randomized simulation (raftsim) plus fault-injection mutation testing of the simulator itself
  • kvraft: driving the pure Member state machine from a 100 ms clock task and asynchronous gRPC dispatch
  • empirical failover measurement (probe): recovering from leader SIGKILL in 1.05 s with zero lost writes

4.1 Server Roles, Terms, and Consensus Invariants

Every replica in a Raft shard runs identical code with symmetric startup arguments; no host is statically designated as leader. At any instant, each member occupies one of three roles: Follower (passive responder granting votes and appending leader batches), Candidate (transient state requesting majority votes after an election timeout), or Leader (sole writer replicating logs and broadcasting heartbeats). Figure 4-1 maps the complete server role state machine and its monotonic term transitions.

Logical time advances in discrete, strictly increasing terms starting at 1. Each term opens with an election; if a candidate secures votes from a majority of members, it leads for the remainder of that term. If votes split without a majority, the term ends with no leader and a new election starts in the next term. Building on the four replication invariants of Chapter 3, we enforce three consensus safety invariants:

No.Consensus InvariantProof Mechanism
0Election Safety: At most one member leads any given term.Each member persists at most one vote per term; any two majorities intersect in at least one member, preventing two candidates from both winning a majority.
1Leader Completeness: Every elected leader holds every record acknowledged in any earlier term.Enforced by the log-completeness voting predicate ((last_term, last_sequence) comparison) combined with quorum intersection.
2Log Safety: A member truncates a log entry only if that entry was never committed.Guaranteed by Leader Completeness together with an explicit runtime guard in Member::truncate against index <= committed.

4.2 Protocol Extension: RequestVote and previous_term

Automated election adds one new gRPC service (Election::RequestVote) and extends the existing AppendRequest message from Chapter 3 with two backward-compatible fields (previous_term as field 6 and leader as field 7). Listing 4.1 defines the Election service in proto/store.proto, and Listing 4.2 presents the evolved Replication service carrying fields 6 and 7 without renumbering any existing fields.

Listing 4.1 Election gRPC service definition in proto/store.proto. proto/store.proto

// Sent by a candidate to every other member of the shard.
service Election {
  rpc RequestVote(VoteRequest) returns (VoteResponse);
}

message VoteRequest {
  uint64 term = 1;
  uint32 candidate = 2;
  // The end of the candidate's log, and the term of its last record.
  uint64 last_sequence = 3;
  uint64 last_term = 4;
}

message VoteResponse {
  uint64 term = 1;
  bool granted = 2;
}

Listing 4.2 Backward-compatible evolution of Replication in proto/store.proto. proto/store.proto

// Sent by the leader of a shard to each follower.
service Replication {
  // Appends records to the follower's log. A call with no records is a
  // heartbeat: it tells the follower that the leader is alive.
  rpc Append(AppendRequest) returns (AppendResponse);
}

message AppendRequest {
  // The shard, named by the last position it owns.
  fixed64 shard = 1;
  // The term of the sender. A follower rejects a leader of an older term.
  uint64 term = 2;
  // The sequence of the record that precedes `records` in the leader's log.
  uint64 previous_sequence = 3;
  repeated Record records = 4;
  // Every record up to this sequence is on a majority of the replicas.
  uint64 committed_sequence = 5;
  // Added for leader election. The term of the record at previous_sequence,
  // and the id of the sender.
  uint64 previous_term = 6;
  uint32 leader = 7;
}

message AppendResponse {
  uint64 term = 1;
  // False when the follower's log does not end at `previous_sequence`.
  bool appended = 2;
  // The sequence of the last record in the follower's log.
  uint64 last_sequence = 3;
}

Following the pure-library pattern of Chapter 3, raft/src/lib.rs defines transport-independent domain message types. Listing 4.3 declares the kv and filesystem imports of raft/src/lib.rs, and Listing 4.4 specifies the addressed Envelope and Message enum covering Append, Appended, RequestVote, and Voted.

Listing 4.3 Imports of raft/src/lib.rs. raft/src/lib.rs

use std::fs::{self, File};
use std::io::{self, Write};

use kv::{Change, Condition, Entry, Log, Record, StoreError, apply, check};

pub type NodeId = u32;

/// Sent by a leader to a follower.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct AppendRequest {
    pub term: u64,
    pub leader: NodeId,
    /// The sequence of the record that precedes `records`, and its term.
    pub previous_sequence: u64,
    pub previous_term: u64,
    pub records: Vec<Record>,
    pub committed_sequence: u64,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct AppendAnswer {
    pub term: u64,
    pub from: NodeId,
    pub appended: bool,
    /// When appended: the last sequence that is known to match the leader's
    /// log. When refused: the sequence the leader should continue from.
    pub last_sequence: u64,
}

/// Sent by a candidate to every other member.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct VoteRequest {
    pub term: u64,
    pub candidate: NodeId,
    /// The end of the candidate's log, and the term of its last record.
    pub last_sequence: u64,
    pub last_term: u64,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct VoteAnswer {
    pub term: u64,
    pub from: NodeId,
    pub granted: bool,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Message {
    Append(AppendRequest),
    Appended(AppendAnswer),
    Vote(VoteRequest),
    Voted(VoteAnswer),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Outgoing {
